sections.name: Cynthia G.

sections.heading: Homes, Businesses and Industrial Sites, One Wichita Office
body: ElectriCraft works out of 1218 E 18th St North in Wichita. For homes, the work customers describe runs from a single bathroom receptacle to a rebuilt service drop line. The same company lists commercial electrical installation and industrial electrical repairs.
Residential electrical services come with a one-year warranty, and ElectriCraft describes itself as a licensed and insured company. The office is open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.

sections.heading: A Panel Updated and a New Garage Wired
body: Billie V. had her panel updated and her new garage wired. She wrote that it was not her first call to ElectriCraft, and would not be her last.

image.alt: Electrical panel with breakers and labeled circuits

sections.quote: Jimmy and his crew were very efficient and knowledgeable. Everything looks so much nicer. They don't leave a huge mess, they are very cleanly. They are polite and will make good on a job! We appreciate them so much. We are highly satisfied with our new breaker box.
sections.name: Vera W.

sections.heading: A Live Line Sagging Over His Garage Roof for Over a Month
body: Jim H.'s service drop line was damaged in a severe storm. He wrote that the utility left a live line sagging across his garage roof for over a month. ElectriCraft rebuilt the damaged riser, ran new conductors and installed a new weatherhead and mast kit.

He wrote that the office pushed the utility's dispatch on his behalf through weeks of delays, and that ElectriCraft wrote off an extra call-out fee those delays had caused. He described the work as compliant with city code.

image.alt: Electrician working at a meter box on a brick wall

sections.quote: He was very thorough, knowledgeable, and professional. He addressed all of the concerns that the buyers requested we fix and even found another issue that the inspector didn't catch. It only took 2 hours and the price was very reasonable!
sections.name: Catherine S.

sections.heading: A Trench Backfilled and an Inspection That Was Almost a Formality
body: Mike D. wanted power extended to a new shed. The electrician who came to estimate showed a strong interest in what he needed, asked questions and offered options that would save him money.

He scheduled the job a day later, and the crew arrived and started on time. Where wires and outlets could be routed more than one way, he was given options. He wrote that yard damage was kept to a minimum, the conduit trench was backfilled and the city inspection was almost a formality.

sections.heading: Outlets for Verdant Coven Plant Co.
body: Eva T. had ElectriCraft install outlets while her plant shop, Verdant Coven Plant Co., was being built out. She wrote that the electrician went above and beyond in every way possible.
She wrote that he pays attention to detail and takes pride in his work, and that with so many moving parts to juggle, having someone reliable and knowledgeable made a real difference.

sections.heading: Fox & Hound and a Facility: The Commercial Side
body: Thomas M. has had multiple jobs done at both his residence and his place of business. Jerry W. has used ElectriCraft at his facility and wrote that the communication is excellent and the work is good and affordable.

ElectriCraft's site lists commercial electrical installation, including emergency lighting, with past projects at Fox & Hound Restaurant and Ultimate Electronics. Industrial work is listed as electrical repairs.

sections.heading: Two Home Generators, Two Brands
body: Matt B. had ElectriCraft troubleshoot an error code on a Kohler generator, and his father has used the company for years. When a storm knocked out power, the office scheduled next-day service so the generator would keep running.

Edwin Z. had a Briggs & Stratton home generator worked on. He wrote that the electrician told him it was a brand he had never worked on before, and that a year later the unit comes on weekly, uses no oil and has given him no problems.

ElectriCraft describes itself as a licensed and insured company.

items.q: Do you only work on houses?
items.a: No. ElectriCraft also does commercial electrical installation, including emergency lighting, and industrial electrical repairs.

sections.quote: Working with Electricraft was so easy. From scheduling to service completion, they were informative, polite, and professional. The technician explained why certain things had stopped working, what needed to be done, some things we needed to be aware of in an older house, and finished the job in no time. They'll be our first call if another problem arises. Also: AFFORDABLE.
sections.name: Lauren D.

sections.heading: Lights That Went Out, Many Issues at Once
body: Anna J. called when some of her lights went out. The electrician came by to check things out and was on time for the appointment, which she wrote was amazing since other services often keep you waiting. She was relieved to have things up and working again.
Julie K. had many issues and appreciated ElectriCraft coming right out on a Sunday. She wrote that Jimmy fixed them all.

sections.name: Nick B.

sections.heading: A $4,200 Quote and a $400 Fix
body: Hope S. was quoted $4,200 by another electric company. She called ElectriCraft, and Matthew checked out the issue and fixed it. The cost was $400.
She wrote that she could not be more pleased with the expertise and integrity of the company.

sections.heading: Several Visits Since Starting a 1910 Bungalow Restoration
body: Danny L. has had Julian out several times since he began restoring his 1910 bungalow. He wrote that the work has been excellent and that Julian knows a lot about how they used to do things back in the day.
Danny plans to have him back out as the restoration continues, and he recommends both the electrician and the company.

sections.heading: Single Digits Outside, an Uninsulated Attic Inside
body: Rebecca's job was large, and the temperatures outside were in the single digits. She wrote that the crew worked in the uninsulated attic, the basement and all the spots in between, and that they communicated from an ETA of 20 minutes through the entire process.
She also wrote that the company helped her plan the work as smaller budget items she could schedule out and mark off, so she felt she was progressing.

sections.heading: A Tree Down and the Utility Waiting on the Meter
body: A huge tree landed in Taryn S.'s yard and knocked out power lines. She wrote that the utility would not restore power unless the meter was fixed, and that when she asked for urgency, Jimmy and his son made it happen quickly and efficiently.
They also called the utility to confirm that replacing the meter box was all it needed to replace the power lines.

sections.heading: A New Outlet and Damaged Wiring Outside His Parents' House
body: Jeffrey P. had ElectriCraft install a new outlet and repair damaged wiring outside at his parents' house. He wrote that the guys did an excellent job for his parents.

sections.heading: Calling Back for Years
body: Lydia P. has had ElectriCraft do work in her house for years, from remodeling projects to repair work, and calls them her first go-to. Phyllis C. has called them over the past seven years for different issues.
Copp M. has hired ElectriCraft for several projects in their home over several years, and William M. has used them twice, most recently the day he wrote.

sections.heading: Knew What It Was, Fixed It, Came in Under Budget
body: les F. wrote that the electrician knew exactly what the problem was and fixed it quickly. Lorenzo S. wrote about good work diagnosing and fixing their electrical issues. David S. had his home electrical issues fixed and was happy with the job.
Matt S. wrote that the job came in under budget and that he will use ElectriCraft again.

sections.heading: Four More Wafer Lights, a Stair Light and a Wet Bar GFCI

He added that Kathy at the office was professional and friendly, and that if you want a job done right, you should give them a call.

sections.heading: Vaulted Ceiling Lights, an Elevated TV Outlet and Dimmers
body: Jennifer D. hired ElectriCraft three times in less than a year. They added ceiling lights to a vaulted ceiling, installed an elevated outdoor TV outlet, and added multiple indoor outlets and dimmer switches.

She wrote that scheduling was thorough and transparent, and that the installations look great and function perfectly. Having lived in four states in five years, she called Jimmy the best electrician she has encountered.

sections.heading: Sconces, and a Bathroom Exhaust Fan Installed by Two Electricians
body: Lynn W. had Jimmy come to her home and install sconces. She wrote that he was friendly and efficient and did a great job.
Kathy G. had a bathroom exhaust fan put in by Jimmy and Shawn. She wrote that they were quick and did a fantastic job, and that she will be calling them back for more electrical work.

sections.heading: The Property Inspector Recommended Them Over Anyone in Town
body: Kassandra B. had ElectriCraft put an exhaust fan in her bathroom and upgrade her panel. She wrote that the inspector for the property highly recommended ElectriCraft over anyone in town, and that she was glad they did. She called the crew friendly and professional through and through.

sections.heading: A Breaker Box Moved, With Lights Installed in the Same Job
body: Taylor R. had a breaker box relocated and updated, and had some lights installed or reinstalled. Taylor wrote that everyone was kind and knowledgeable, that they are super easy to get ahold of and that the pricing seemed reasonable.
Taylor also wrote that ElectriCraft will be their go-to for any electrical needs in the future.

sections.heading: A Call Ahead for an Unexpected Schedule
body: Elizabeth wrote that the electrician called ahead and was willing to work with her unexpected schedule. There was clear communication when they discussed the installation of the lights.
When the job was done he cleaned up, and she found the price very reasonable.

sections.heading: Options You May Not Have Thought Of
body: Martin N. wrote that Jimmy takes the time to thoroughly understand your needs, offers options you may not have thought of, and takes time to explain his completed work.

sections.heading: An Extra Bathroom Receptacle and Lighting for All Her Needs
body: Kelley N. had an additional receptacle put in her bathroom. She wrote that the crew showed up on time and cleaned up when they finished.

footer.about: ElectriCraft is a Wichita electrical company serving homes, commercial buildings and industrial sites. We repair, install and upgrade.
why: Weekdays 7 to 5 at 1218 E 18th St North

Your site is laid out at desktop width, so on a phone a visitor scrolls sideways to read it, and your homepage has an empty main headline. Someone at a warm outlet with a phone in hand can't see what you do.

Your reviews describe an electrician who tells people what else they found: wiring that needed protecting, something an inspector missed, what to know about an older house. Today those words sit on Google, not on your site.
So the demo tells one story on every page. It opens with Electrician in Wichita, KS, and gives electrical repair and lighting installation a page each, because your site has no page for either.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Electrician People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page of the demo.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: Where Google learns who you are and where you work.
problems: Your homepage has an empty H1. The visible headline, “It's Watt Your Home Needs!”, isn't the H1, so Google can't tell what you are or where.
The copy is general, so it doesn't say what makes a call to you different.
fixes: A headline that says Electrician in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
A page built around what you do on a repair call: fix it, then tell people what else you see.

cards.title: Electrical Repair
cards.why: When an outlet is warm or a breaker keeps tripping, people call the first company they find.
problems: Repair sits inside one long page titled “Residential Electricians in Wichita, KS,” so “electrical repair Wichita KS” has nothing built for it.
fixes: A page for electrical repair in Wichita, KS: what the signs mean, what happens when you call, and when a repair points to something bigger.
cards.alsoAdd: Rebuilt panel upgrade, generator service, and meter box and service line repair pages, each built for its own search.

cards.title: Lighting Installation
cards.why: Fan and lighting jobs are searched for by name.
problems: Your site has no page for lighting installation, so “lighting installation Wichita KS” has nothing built for it.
fixes: A page for lighting installation in Wichita, KS: fans, recessed lights, sconces and dimmers, and what goes into each.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a customer with a dead outlet decides to call.
problems: Your residential FAQ promises 24/7 emergency service while your hours say Monday to Friday, 7 to 5, so a caller at night can't tell whether anyone will answer.
None of your form's five fields is marked required.
fixes: Your address, hours and both numbers together on one page.
One honest line on after-hours calls: call and ask.
A short list of what to have ready when you call.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already describe the company you are. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we’ll walk you through this demo and what a full build adds.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your homepage description says over 30 years, your residential FAQ says over 20 years and your panel page says since 1984, so which number should every listing use?

Your residential FAQ promises 24/7 emergency service, while every page footer says Monday to Friday, 7 to 5 with weekends closed, so which hours should Google show, and how should after-hours callers reach you?
Your site lists 1218 E 18th St North in Wichita, while a BBB listing we found shows a Haysville headquarters, so which address should every listing use?
Your footer prints Kansas Contractor Lic# 1399, but we couldn't check it against a Kansas or Wichita lookup, so what is the license type, and whose name is it under?

lead.heading: Why we led with what your electricians point out
lead.text: We led with what customers say happens after the fix because it lives only in your reviews. Two customers each wrote that the electrician found more than the job they called about, and a generic electrician site can't copy that.

rows.claim: Fix the problem, then tell you plainly what else we see
Storm damage to the meter box or service line, handled with you and the utility
